JNJ.rationale: JNJ's fundamental health is solid but not improving: normalized EPS is flat at ~$2.14/quarter, net margins have contracted 550bp (from 27.3% to 21.8%), and ROE has declined from 31.7% to 25.9%. The Q2 2026 beat ($25.31B revenue, $2.90 adjusted EPS, raised guidance to $101.1B/$11.68) is a genuine positive, but the stock has already re-rated from 18x to 29x P/E on flat normalized earnings—entirely multiple expansion, not earnings growth. At 29x, the 3.4% earnings yield underperforms the 10-year Treasury at 4.57%, meaning the market is paying a premium over risk-free for a mid-single-digit grower with compressing margins. The Stelara biosimilar headwind (760bps on Innovative Medicine, 460bps total) is being partially absorbed by Tremfya (+73%) and oncology (+17%), but the FTC antitrust filing (2026-06-23) adds new regulatory tail risk beyond natural biosimilar erosion. Talc litigation remains an unresolved binary risk with a $3.8B reserve that could prove inadequate. Abiomed's 2% sales decline reverses prior 14% growth, signaling potential acquisition-thesis erosion. The deliberate absence from GLP-1/obesity means JNJ misses one of pharma's largest secular growth opportunities. All three pillars align negatively: (1) stable-but-flat fundamentals with margin compression and multiple risk factors, (2) valuation at 97th percentile of 1-year P/E range with no earnings cushion vs. risk-free rate, (3) no credible near-term re-rating catalyst—the Q2 beat is already priced in and the stock pulled back ~2% post-earnings. The price has outrun the business.
